UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
DISTRICT OF WESTBROOK

MAYA T. ELLIS,
                Plaintiff,
        v.                              Case No. 24-CV-04412
CITY OF MARION HEIGHTS;
OFFICER R. DOWLING, in his individual capacity;
OFFICER P. ESQUIVEL, in her individual capacity,
                Defendants.

COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES — 42 U.S.C. § 1983

Plaintiff MAYA T. ELLIS, by and through counsel, alleges as follows:

JURISDICTION AND VENUE
1. This action arises under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 and the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments to the United States Constitution. Jurisdiction is proper under 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331, 1343.

PARTIES
2. Plaintiff Maya T. Ellis is a Black woman, 29 years old, and a resident of Marion Heights, Westbrook.
3. Defendant City of Marion Heights is a municipal corporation.
4. Defendants Dowling and Esquivel are sworn officers of the Marion Heights Police Department, acting under color of state law.

FACTS
5. On June 7, 2024, at approximately 9:14 p.m., Plaintiff was walking her dog along the public sidewalk on Cedar Street near her apartment at 1820 Cedar.
6. Defendants Dowling and Esquivel, in marked patrol unit MHPD-44, stopped Plaintiff without warrant or probable cause. Defendant Dowling stated, "We've had complaints about people loitering in this neighborhood."
7. Plaintiff identified herself, produced ID, and stated she lived two doors down. Defendant Dowling refused to release her and ordered her to sit on the curb.
8. When Plaintiff calmly asked the basis for her detention, Defendant Esquivel grabbed Plaintiff's left arm, twisted it behind her back, and forced her to the pavement face-first.
9. Plaintiff sustained a fractured left wrist (confirmed by Marion Heights Hospital ER, see Exhibit B), facial abrasions, and a torn rotator cuff.
10. Plaintiff was held in handcuffs for approximately 47 minutes. No charges were filed. No incident report was generated for 11 days.
11. Plaintiff has subsequently learned that Marion Heights PD has been sued 14 times in the past five years for excessive force, with 9 of those cases involving Black residents. The City has not disciplined any officer involved.

CLAIMS FOR RELIEF
Count I — Fourth Amendment Excessive Force (Esquivel)
Count II — Fourth Amendment Unlawful Seizure (Dowling, Esquivel)
Count III — Monell Liability (City of Marion Heights) — policy of inadequate training and pattern of unaddressed excessive-force complaints, Monell v. Dep't of Social Services, 436 U.S. 658 (1978).

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff demands compensatory damages, punitive damages against the individual defendants, attorney's fees under 42 U.S.C. § 1988, and such other relief as the Court deems just.

JURY TRIAL DEMANDED.

Dated: July 22, 2024
                                /s/ J. Okafor, Esq.
                                Westbrook Civil Rights Project
